title: PGO-driven batch autotuner and mixed-mode interaction runner
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add a profile-guided batch-size autotuner and a mixed-mode workload runner to better simulate concurrent interactive and bulk inference patterns. Improves throughput in mixed workloads and provides visualization exports for batch-size heatmaps.
description:
Motivation: Selecting a single static micro-batch size for inference is suboptimal for heterogeneous workloads that mix short interactive chats and larger bulk jobs. This PR introduces a profile-guided optimization (PGO) step that collects short workload traces, infers an optimal per-model/per-sequence-length micro-batch policy, and applies it during serving experiments. Additionally, a mixed-mode interaction runner reproduces concurrent interactive + batch traffic to surface cross-workload interference and informs tuning.

What I changed (high level):
- pgo/autotuner: a new binary that runs lightweight traces against a local runtime snapshot, builds a per-model batch policy, and emits a compact policy artifact. The tuner uses a cost model combining latency SLO violation risk and token cost.
- runners/mixed_mode_runner: a runner that composes two traffic forks (interactive short-turns and bulk sequence batches) with configurable mixing ratio, priming sequences, and KV cache warmup. It emits per-request metadata (seq_len, is_interactive, applied_batch) so reports can correlate decisions.
- reporting/batch_heatmap_exporter: exporter that ingests runner telemetry and emits a per-model batch-size heatmap (CSV + compact JSON) and time-series summaries suitable for our benchmarking dashboards.
- small runtime hooks: added an opt-in runtime hook to accept a batch-policy artifact for experiments and a lightweight sampling probe for actual applied micro-batch sizes.

Commit summary: 5 commits; squash on merge. High-level commit messages included below in the commits field.

Files changed (high level):
- pgo/autotuner/{main.rs,policy.rs,cost_model.rs} - new autotuner and cost model
- runners/mixed_mode_runner/{runner.go,config.yaml,sample_workloads/} - new runner and sample payloads
- reporting/batch_heatmap_exporter/{exporter.py,templates/heatmap.csv.j2} - new exporter
- runtime/hooks/{batch_policy_provider.cc,batch_policy.proto} - experimental hook & proto
- tests/{pgo_integration_test.sh,mixed_mode_integration_test.go,ci-flaky-retry.yaml} - integration tests and CI retry rules

Review conversation (condensed):
- Marco: Requested clearer invariants for when the runtime will override the policy (response: added explicit "policy_overrides" config and unit tests to assert precedence).
- Sofia: Asked for guardrails around the cost model to avoid pathological choices for very short sequences (response: introduced a min-batch cap and a fallback heuristic that prefers latency-first under p95 breach).
- Devon: Noted a potential race in the sampling probe when multiple workers report simultaneously; added a per-worker buffer and dedup logic (see runtime/hooks changes).
- Author replies: addressed comments in-line, pushed fixes, and updated tests.

CI: Initial CI run showed two flaky integration tests failing under emulator (timing-sensitive). I adjusted the test harness to use deterministic clocks and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed (unit: pass, integration: pass, fmt/lint: pass).

Benchmark summary (local lab):
- Workload: mixed-mode (80% interactive short-turns, 20% bulk batches, average seq_len_interactive=18, seq_len_bulk=420)
- Baseline (static micro-batch=8): throughput 1250 samples/min, p95 latency 420ms, token-cost baseline 1.00x
- With PGO policy (auto-picked micro-batch per seq bucket): throughput 1740 samples/min (+39%), p95 latency 410ms (-2.4%), token-cost 0.86x (-14%)
- Observations: improved throughput and unit cost without materially increasing p95; improvement predominantly driven by allowing larger micro-batches for bulk sequences while preserving small batches for interactive paths.

Merge: Squash-and-merge after final CI green and reviewers approved.

Notes/follow-ups:
- Next: integrate policy artifact storage into the model-registry so experiments can be replayed across clusters (ENG-2071).
- Add long-running A/B test on dedicated pools to validate at scale and ensure no cross-tenant regressions.
